stories.head: Coca-Cola's Indian bottling parent files IPO papers; Thums Up and Maaza maker's revenue up 20%
stories.dek: Hindustan Coca-Cola Holdings has filed draft papers with SEBI for a share sale of up to about 99.7 crore shares. Coca-Cola's stake would fall from 60% to roughly 45%.

sections.title: What happened
paras: Hindustan Coca-Cola Holdings Ltd (HCCH), the parent of Coca-Cola's India bottling business, filed its draft red herring prospectus with SEBI on 6 November. The issue is entirely an offer for sale of up to 99,74,61,456 shares by Hindustan Coca-Cola Overseas Holdings, so the company itself gets no money from it. Price and rupee size are not out yet, and the shares are meant to list on BSE and NSE.
Seven banks are managing the deal, including Kotak Mahindra Capital, Citigroup, JP Morgan, Morgan Stanley, Axis Capital, Goldman Sachs and IIFL.

sections.title: The business
paras: HCCH runs through Hindustan Coca-Cola Beverages, which sells in 10 states and four Union Territories, mainly in the south and west. It reaches about 17 lakh retail outlets through 2,273 distributors, with 14 production plants, eight co-packing units and 90 bottling lines. Its 41 drinks include Thums Up, Maaza and Kinley.
For April–June 2026 it reported revenue of ₹4,310.17 crore, up 20.46%, with volumes up 18.61% and an EBITDA margin of 17.2% against 13.76% a year earlier.

sections.title: Who owns what
paras: The Coca-Cola Company holds 60% and Jubilant Beverages, which came in during 2025, holds 40%. After the sale Coca-Cola is expected to hold about 45% while Jubilant's stake stays the same. The DRHP values the ready-to-drink market in these states at ₹63,730 crore in FY26 and expects it to reach ₹1.18 lakh crore by FY31.

facts: Offer: up to 99.75 crore shares, all OFS

stories.head: Swiggy renames itself 'Sweety' for Diwali, down to the delivery bags
stories.dek: For the festive season the food-delivery brand has swapped its name on hoardings, rider jerseys, bags and social handles to celebrate India's love of mithai.

sections.title: What Swiggy did
paras: Swiggy has temporarily rebranded itself as 'Sweety' for a Diwali campaign built around mithai. The new name appears on outdoor hoardings, delivery partners' jerseys and bags, and its social media handles, and delivery partners' names in the app carry a 'Sweety' prefix for the campaign period.
The hoardings play on the 'Sweety' nickname with the line 'Sweety Sweety Sweety, mujhe log bolein'. Trade coverage dates the launch to around 5–6 November.

sections.title: Why now
paras: Swiggy's brand VP Mayur Hola said the idea is aimed at capturing the festive pulse of consumer behaviour, with a seasonal jump in mithai orders.

Marketers are split on the value. One branding consultant, Tanurupa Pal, calls this kind of temporary rebrand 'chatter-branding': cheap and good at starting conversations, but it only lasts if it fits what the brand stands for.

facts: Name change covers hoardings, jerseys, bags, social handles
Campaign line: 'Sweety Sweety Sweety, mujhe log bolein'

stories.head: Meesho closes its ₹186.71 crore Kirana Club deal, adding 4.1 million kirana shops
stories.dek: The e-commerce company now owns 92.74% of the kirana-network app and its Indian arm, as it pushes into business-to-business trade outside the big cities.
stat: registered kirana retailers on Kirana Club

sections.title: What happened
paras: Meesho Limited has completed the first and second tranches of its purchase of Kirana Club Pte Ltd and Retail Pulse Labs Pvt Ltd, taking 92.74% for a total of ₹186.71 crore in cash. Kirana Club is now a direct subsidiary and Retail Pulse Labs, its Indian operating arm, is a step-down subsidiary.
The share purchase agreement was signed on 12 June 2026. On 28 October Meesho's board also approved follow-on investments of $650,000 in Kirana Club and ₹18.74 crore in Retail Pulse Labs.

sections.title: Why it matters
paras: Kirana Club gives Meesho access to more than 4.1 million registered kirana retailers, mostly in smaller towns. Meesho says the deal widens its asset-light B2B presence across non-metro India and takes it into general trade.
Kirana Club is expected to keep running independently within the group. The ₹202 crore figure seen in earlier headlines was the originally announced plan, before the deal closed at 92.74%.

stories.head: Ramayana: Part One crosses ₹200 crore gross in India in three days
stories.dek: Nitesh Tiwari's Diwali release, starring Ranbir Kapoor and Yash, is at ₹208 crore gross after its first weekend day, though Hindi screens are running at only 35% full.

sections.title: The numbers
paras: According to The Week, which cites Sacnilk for the latest day, Ramayana: Part One stands at about ₹208.01 crore gross and ₹174.94 crore net in India after three days. Day 1 brought ₹64.85 crore net, Day 2 dipped to ₹48.05 crore, and Day 3 was tracking ₹62.04 crore net by 9 pm. Day-3 figures are provisional and different trackers differ.
Worldwide, the film had ₹230.05 crore through Day 2, including ₹95.25 crore from overseas.

sections.title: Where it is strong
paras: Hindi gave about 75% of Day-3 net, ₹48.33 crore, but at only 35.1% occupancy. The smaller markets are fuller: Tamil 76.3%, Kannada 64.7% and Telugu 53%.
Trade coverage calls Sunday the real test of whether the weekend holds. The film is described as one of the biggest releases in Bollywood's Diwali history, with Sai Pallavi as Sita.

stories.head: 10 years after demonetisation, cash in circulation is at a record ₹43.46 lakh crore
stories.dek: The 8 November 2016 note ban was meant to curb black money and push digital payments. UPI exploded, but India's cash habit survived.
stat: currency in circulation, highest in 5 years

sections.title: Cash did not go away
paras: Business Standard reports that currency in circulation reached ₹43.46 lakh crore on 15 October, its highest in five years. On the eve of the ban it was ₹17.74 lakh crore, so cash is now roughly 2.5 times that level. Cash relative to the size of the economy has returned to about where it was before 8 November 2016.
The RBI's latest household survey still records a 'continued strong preference' for cash.

sections.title: But UPI changed how India pays
paras: Onmanorama reports that UPI now runs at more than 25 billion transactions a month worth over ₹31 trillion, a world away from its small start in 2016.

The government's stated aims were curbing black money and counterfeit notes, and on those the evidence is still debated. Newspaper editorials today argue that a full accounting of what the exercise achieved is still owed.

stories.head: DeepMind's AI agents find two weaknesses in legacy 1024-bit RSA
stories.dek: Google DeepMind says human-guided AI agents cut the theoretical cost of forging some RSA signatures by about 1,600x. Modern 2048-bit keys are not affected.
stat: theoretical gain on short-digest signature forgery

sections.title: What DeepMind found
paras: Google DeepMind announced on 6 November that human-guided AI agents helped find two weaknesses in legacy 1024-bit RSA. The first targets signatures made over short fingerprints and is estimated to be about 1,600 times more efficient at forgery. The second lowers the marginal cost of each extra key in a large batch factoring attack by about 30 times.
The signature gain is a theoretical estimate for 1024-bit keys and was not run at full size. The paper is titled 'Forging 1024-bit RSA signatures in nearly SNFS time' and is on IACR.

sections.title: Should you worry?
paras: DeepMind's Pushmeet Kohli said the results only affect obsolete 1024-bit systems, and that modern protocols, which almost universally use 2048-bit or larger keys, remain secure. Security teams are still being urged to audit any leftover 1024-bit keys. Figures here come from press coverage of the announcement and have not been checked against the paper.

facts: Batch factoring: ~30x cheaper per extra key

stories.credit: OYO Hotel Praia de Ondina / Wikimedia, CC BY-SA 4.0
stories.head: OYO parent PRISM posts ₹353 crore Q1 profit, but ₹244 crore is a tax credit
stories.dek: Revenue rose 35% to ₹2,814 crore, yet most of the profit growth comes from a one-off deferred tax credit rather than cash from hotels.

sections.title: The results
paras: PRISM, the parent of OYO, reported a consolidated profit after tax of ₹353 crore for April–June 2026 (Q1 FY27), up 17% from ₹301 crore a year earlier. Revenue grew 35% to ₹2,814 crore, EBITDA rose 24% to ₹760 crore and gross booking value climbed about 30% to nearly ₹9,600 crore.

sections.title: Read the fine print
paras: The reported profit includes a deferred tax credit of about ₹244 crore, which is an accounting item and not cash earned from running hotels, so the ₹353 crore should not be read as operating cash profit. The figures come from audited financials seen by PTI.
PRISM, which renamed itself from Oravel Stays, is IPO-bound. Its shareholders have approved a ₹6,650 crore fresh issue.

stories.head: New-age scorecard: Nykaa profit jumps 207%, Lenskart doubles, Swiggy's loss narrows
stories.dek: Three consumer-internet names reported July–September results. Two are solidly profitable now, while Swiggy is still losing money but less than last year.

sections.title: The three results
paras: Nykaa's profit after tax rose 207% year on year to about ₹101 crore on revenue of roughly ₹3,006 crore, up 28%, with fashion turning profitable.
Lenskart's profit roughly doubled, to about ₹227–232 crore depending on the report, on revenue of about ₹2,845 crore.
Swiggy's consolidated loss narrowed to ₹922 crore from ₹1,092 crore a year earlier.

sections.title: What to watch
paras: Reports give slightly different revenue numbers for Swiggy and different growth rates for Lenskart, so check company filings for exact figures. The common thread is that scale is finally turning into profit for beauty and eyewear, while quick commerce still needs heavy spending.

stories.head: Delhi's air hits AQI 369 on Diwali eve, with 'severe' forecast for today and tomorrow
stories.dek: Sixteen of 59 monitoring stations were already in the severe band on Saturday, and experts warn some could cross 450 after tonight's fireworks.

sections.title: Where things stand
paras: Delhi's average air quality index was 369 on Saturday, in the 'very poor' band, with 16 of 59 stations in 'severe'. The worst reading was around 452 near IIT Delhi. One outlet reported a different figure of 391 earlier in the week, so numbers vary by source.
The Early Warning System expects 'severe' air on 8 and 9 November.

sections.title: Crackers and rules
paras: Limited green-cracker windows applied on 7 and 8 November, with a full ban returning on 9 November. Reports say unlicensed fireworks were still on sale in Old Delhi.
Experts warn the 24-hour reading could worsen after Diwali, as it did in past years despite 'green' crackers, with stubble fires adding to the load.

stories.head: Agniveers get two more years: Cabinet clears a 'second tour of duty'
stories.dek: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh said willing Agniveers can stay on and be enrolled as regular soldiers after four or six years if they meet selection criteria.

sections.title: What changed
paras: The Union Cabinet cleared a two-year extension, called a 'Second Tour of Duty', for Agniveers, and Rajnath Singh announced it on 4 November. It is meant for the roughly 75% who would otherwise have left after four years.
Singh said willing Agniveers can be enrolled as regular soldiers after four or six years of service if they qualify, and officials said the scheme itself has not been rolled back.

sections.title: Open questions
paras: Coverage differs on the details: some outlets say only the 25% selected on merit are absorbed directly while the rest get the extension option, others describe the whole cohort as eligible for regular enrolment.
Reports also mention higher pay and a bigger Seva Nidhi package, while AIMIM's Asaduddin Owaisi has asked whether extended Agniveers will get the same benefits as regular soldiers.

stories.head: Peppermint Robotics raises ₹100 crore to scale robots worldwide
stories.dek: The Pune and Austin-based startup closed a pre-Series B led by pi Ventures and Crane Venture Partners, roughly $10.5 million.

sections.title: The round
paras: Peppermint Robotics has raised about ₹100 crore (around $10.5 million) in a pre-Series B round led by pi Ventures and Crane Venture Partners, with Asiana Fund also taking part. The round mixes fresh capital with secondary share sales.
CEO Runal Dahiwade said the money will go to global expansion, engineering, product development and capex.

sections.title: Background
paras: The company last raised a ₹34 crore Series A in April 2025 from JDSS, Enrission India Capital, Indian Angel Network and Vinners, which took its total funding to about ₹49 crore. It was one of three growth-stage deals in a week when Indian startups raised $255–258 million, more than double the week before.

facts: Leads: pi Ventures, Crane Venture Partners

stories.head: Starlink India still hasn't launched, and the ₹8,600 price was test data
stories.dek: Despite its licence and a Jio distribution deal, Starlink was not taking consumer orders in India as of 6 November.

sections.title: Where things stand
paras: Starlink is licensed to operate in India, but there is still no confirmed launch date or official Indian price. As of 6 November it was not available for consumer orders.
Its arrangement with Jio is a distribution agreement, not a live service.

sections.title: The price that wasn't
paras: The ₹8,600 a month plan and ₹34,000 hardware kit that many articles quote briefly appeared on Starlink's India website in December 2025. The company later said they were dummy figures shown by mistake, so any story presenting them as confirmed pricing is out of date.

facts: Status on 6 Nov: no consumer orders

stories.head: LPG check for November: commercial cylinder up ₹10, home cylinder unchanged at ₹942
stories.dek: Petrol and diesel prices are also unchanged, while jet fuel went up ₹1.30 a litre.
stat: 14.2 kg home cylinder in Delhi, unchanged

sections.title: What changed on 1 November
paras: The 19 kg commercial LPG cylinder rose ₹10 in Delhi to ₹2,820, from ₹2,810 the month before. Jet fuel (ATF) rose ₹1.30 per litre.
Retail petrol and diesel rates stayed the same across the country.

sections.title: For your kitchen
paras: Domestic 14.2 kg LPG has been held at ₹942 in Delhi since 7 June 2026. Rules that continue include biometric Aadhaar authentication for LPG and the 30-day cylinder termination rule introduced in May 2026. Check Indian Oil's city-wise page for your exact price.

stories.head: Axon invests $1.2 billion in drone maker Skydio at a $5.2 billion valuation
stories.dek: Only $255 million is fresh capital; the rest buys existing shares. Axon becomes Skydio's exclusive public-safety distributor in the US and Canada.

sections.title: The deal
paras: Axon is investing $1.2 billion in Skydio at a $5.2 billion pre-money valuation, lifting its stake from about 15% to roughly 37%. Only about $255 million is new money for Skydio, with the remainder buying existing shares.
Axon also becomes the exclusive distributor of Skydio drones to public-safety agencies in the US and Canada.

sections.title: Market reaction
paras: Axon's own shares fell about 18% on the day, in a report that also noted a revenue and EPS miss and lower guidance. Axon and Skydio first partnered in 2021, and Axon joined Skydio's 2023 round at a $2.2 billion valuation. The terms come from a small number of reports and should be checked against company filings.

stories.head: US sets up Task Force Iron Gate to extend its Iran blockade to land routes
stories.dek: CENTCOM also disabled another commercial ship in the Gulf of Oman, the 11th since the naval blockade began in July.
stat: ship disabled since the blockade began

sections.title: What CENTCOM announced
paras: US Central Command created Task Force Iron Gate on 7 November, a roughly 20-person unit in Tampa that will target overland and Caspian trade routes not covered by the maritime blockade. Admiral Brad Cooper made the decision.
On Saturday US forces disabled a commercial vessel in the Gulf of Oman after its civilian crew ignored repeated warnings and tried to run the blockade.

sections.title: The wider picture
paras: CENTCOM says the blockade has stopped Iran from exporting more than $25 billion of crude in recent months, a figure that has not been independently verified.
CBS reports the move comes amid a diplomatic push to avoid a new round of major fighting, with Qatar working on a possible deal.

facts: Task force: ~20 people, based in Tampa

stories.head: Wall Street ends its worst week in over a year, even after a Friday bounce
stories.dek: The S&P 500 fell 2.7% for the week and the Nasdaq logged a fourth straight weekly loss, as AI stocks sold off before a partial rebound.

sections.title: Friday's close
paras: On Friday 6 November the S&P 500 rose 0.3% to 7,376.86, the Nasdaq gained 1.1% to 24,579.42 and the Russell 2000 added 0.9% to 2,754.11. The Dow slipped 0.5% to 51,285.73.
Chip stocks led the bounce after Thursday's AI-led rout, and a strong US jobs report (165,000 jobs added) pushed Treasury yields up.

sections.title: The week
paras: For the week the S&P 500 lost 2.7%, its worst in more than a year, the Nasdaq lost 3.4%, its fourth weekly decline in a row, and the Dow fell 0.9%. The S&P is still up 7.8% for 2026 and the Nasdaq up 5.8%. Investors were also dealing with uncertainty around the US midterm elections.

stories.head: Reliance jumps 8% on record Q2; Jio Platforms trades 28% above IPO price
stories.dek: Shares rose on 2 November after Reliance posted record quarterly revenue, EBITDA and profit, taking its market value above ₹17 lakh crore.
stat: Jio Platforms' listing price on 28 Oct

sections.title: Reliance
paras: Reliance Industries shares surged more than 8% on 2 November, lifting its market capitalisation above ₹17 lakh crore, after the company reported record revenue, EBITDA and net profit for the July–September quarter of FY27.

sections.title: Jio Platforms
paras: Jio Platforms listed on 28 October at ₹1,358, a 21.4% premium to the ₹1,119 issue price. After its first results as a listed company it rose as much as 3% on 2 November to ₹1,475 on the NSE. A recent snapshot showed it about 28% above the IPO price, though sources differ on the latest quote.
This is a week-old market move, included because it shaped the rally in Indian stocks that followed.

stories.head: CarTrade leads new-age stocks, up 23% in a week as 54 of 69 tracked names gain
stories.dek: Foreign buying, Q2 earnings and lower crude helped the Inc42 basket, while the Nifty Midcap 100 rose 5.8%.

sections.title: The rally
paras: Inc42 says 54 of the 69 listed new-age tech companies it tracks gained for the week, by between 0.4% and 23.3%. CarTrade topped the list, bouncing 23.3% to ₹2,699.30 after a steep fall the week before.
The Nifty Midcap 100 rose 5.8% and the Smallcap 100 rose 2.8%.

sections.title: Why
paras: Analysts credited returning foreign investor buying, strong Q2 FY27 earnings, easing geopolitical worries and lower crude oil prices. As always with week-long moves, some of the gains follow earlier losses, so they are not a forecast.

stories.head: India win rain-hit 2nd ODI by 4 runs (DLS) to lead New Zealand 2-0
stories.dek: Gurnoor Brar took a career-best 4/30 in Wellington as New Zealand were bowled out for about 134 chasing a revised target.

sections.title: How it ended
paras: India won the second ODI in Wellington by 4 runs on the DLS method after rain stopped play just as New Zealand were mounting a late chase. The hosts were restricted to about 134 in 41 overs, with sources giving 134 or 135, which one report called their lowest ODI total against India at home.
Gurnoor Brar's 4/30 was the standout, with Shreyas Iyer (30) and KL Rahul (26 not out) helping India's innings.

sections.title: Next
paras: India lead the five-match series 2-0. The third ODI is on 10 November at Seddon Park in Hamilton.

stories.head: Dhinidhi Desinghu becomes the first Indian with two Youth Olympics medals
stories.dek: She took bronze in the 200m freestyle in Dakar, while Tirthank Pegu won bronze in the 200m butterfly. India's tally is now six.
stat: India's medals in Dakar so far

sections.title: Friday's medals
paras: Dhinidhi Desinghu won bronze in the women's 200m freestyle at the Youth Olympic Games in Dakar, making her the first Indian to win two medals at the Games. Tirthank Pegu added bronze in the men's 200m butterfly.
Those two took India's total to six: two silver and four bronze.

sections.title: The tally
paras: The earlier medals were Tanvi Patri's badminton silver, Khushbu Darjada's judo silver and Rajkumari Lanchenbi Chanu's wushu bronze. The Games run until 13 November, so the count can still rise.

stories.head: Chennaiyin FC thrash defending champions East Bengal 5-3 in ISL goal-fest
stories.dek: Brison Fernandes scored twice in the first 18 minutes and Irfan Yadwad added two more after the break.

sections.title: The match
paras: Chennaiyin beat East Bengal 5-3 at the Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium in Chennai on Saturday for their first win of ISL 2026-27. Brison Fernandes scored twice inside 18 minutes, Ramon Tanque converted a first-half penalty and Irfan Yadwad scored twice after the break.
East Bengal's goals came from Aké Loba, Dani Ramírez, from a penalty after a handball, and David Lalhlansanga in stoppage time.

sections.title: Why it matters
paras: It was East Bengal's first league defeat of the season. Chennaiyin collected their first three points of the campaign.

facts: East Bengal's first league loss of the season

stories.head: Leeds beat Tottenham 1-0 with a late Noah Okafor goal
stories.dek: The substitute's goal ended Spurs' winning run in Saturday's Premier League action.

sections.title: Saturday's Premier League
paras: Noah Okafor came off the bench to score a late winner as Leeds United beat Tottenham Hotspur 1-0, ending Spurs' winning run.
Elsewhere on the day, Fulham drew 1-1 with Newcastle United, and Sky Sports and CBS Sports both list Arsenal 1-0 Hull City as full time.

stories.head: Suriya's Scene earns ₹81.5 crore worldwide in two days
stories.dek: The Diwali action-comedy added ₹20.25 crore net in India on Saturday, up 5.7% on opening day.

sections.title: The numbers
paras: Sacnilk's tracking puts Scene at about ₹81.50 crore worldwide gross after two days. In India it made ₹20.25 crore net on Saturday, up 5.7% from Friday, taking its two-day India net to ₹39.40 crore.
Great Andhra says the film is expected to cross ₹100 crore worldwide over the opening weekend if the momentum holds.

sections.title: The Diwali clash
paras: Scene opened on 6 November against Ranbir Kapoor and Yash's Ramayana: Part One. Advance bookings were about ₹20 crore across six days, and its Kerala rights were reportedly the highest ever paid for a Suriya film in the state. Trackers' figures are estimates and can change.

stories.head: Godzilla Minus Zero heads for a record $32 million US opening
stories.dek: It would be the biggest ever US opening for a live-action foreign-language film, ahead of The Cat in the Hat.

sections.title: The record
paras: Studio-trade estimates have Godzilla Minus Zero taking about $32 million in its US opening weekend, which would be the biggest for a live-action foreign-language film. The previous best was $17.8 million for 2002's Hero. It would also be distributor GKids' biggest opening ever.
Friday brought about $14.5 million including roughly $6–6.7 million from previews.

sections.title: The competition
paras: The Cat in the Hat was projected at about $18.7 million for second place. Worldwide, the Japanese monster film was tipped for around $60 million. These are estimates from 7 November, and final numbers may differ.

stories.credit: Bangka slow loris / via Good News Network
stories.head: A venomous primate feared extinct for a century is alive in Indonesia
stories.dek: The Bangka slow loris, last recorded in the 1930s, has been found again, thanks largely to a rescue centre's records.
stat: rescued lorises released back to the wild

sections.title: What happened
paras: The Bangka slow loris, a venomous primate listed as 'possibly extinct' in 2015 and last documented by Western science in the 1930s, is still living on Bangka Island in Indonesia. A new paper by Austrian and international researchers confirmed it.
Much of the evidence came from the Alobi Wildlife Rescue Center, which rescued more than 90 of the animals between 2015 and 2025.

sections.title: Why it matters
paras: Alobi released 86 of those lorises back into the wild. Most were found after wandering into gardens, plantations or roads. The records suggest the species lives across more of Bangka than thought, and as one of very few venomous primates it now has a stronger case for protection.

stories.credit: Lordenshaw Hill Fort / The Wildlife Trusts, via Good News Network
stories.head: 25,000 people from 50 countries help buy a 9,400-acre estate for wildlife
stories.dek: The Wildlife Trusts raised about £30 million to protect Rothbury Estate in Northumberland, home to a Bronze Age hill fort.

sections.title: What happened
paras: The Wildlife Trusts has bought Rothbury Estate in Northumberland, England, around 9,400 acres including a Bronze Age hill fort, for about £30 million. More than 25,000 supporters from 50 countries chipped in, alongside funding from the National Lottery Heritage Fund, DEFRA and the Esmée Fairbairn Foundation.

sections.title: Who lives there
paras: The land shelters curlews, lapwings and other wading birds, mountain bumblebees, red squirrels, cuckoos and merlins in the woods, skylarks, salmon and a critically endangered eel.

stories.credit: Berry Fresh Agrotech / via The Better India
stories.head: After a failed first crop, a 57-year-old grew soil-free strawberries and sold ₹44 lakh
stories.dek: Ketan Sodha, a Mumbai commerce graduate with no farming background, now grows strawberries year-round in Mahabaleshwar.
stat: in sales from ~8,000 kg of fruit

sections.title: From disaster to polyhouse
paras: Ketan Sodha, 57, a BCom graduate from Mumbai, started growing strawberries in 2016 with 5,000 plants and called his first year 'a disaster'. He expanded to 10,000 plants in 2017 and by 2020–21 farmed almost 40 acres across three sites.

After touring farms in Italy, Spain, Egypt and Turkey, he built a soilless polyhouse on 2 acres with 19,500 plants in cocopeat, automated fertigation, misting, rainwater harvesting and ozone-treated water.

sections.title: The results
paras: His venture, Berry Fresh Agrotech, reports about 8,000 kg of fruit and ₹44 lakh in sales, at ₹400–600 a kg, about 60% direct to consumers. He is now in talks with investors for a 5-acre farm with at least 200,000 plants.

stories.credit: Transplanted peepal / via The Better India
stories.head: A 100-year-old peepal was lifted by a 50-tonne crane and replanted, and it's growing
stories.dek: Tree-transplantation expert Bharat Sisodia saved an Ahmedabad peepal after it was cut down, moving it nearly two kilometres.
stat: distance the century-old peepal was moved

sections.title: The rescue
paras: When a roughly 100-year-old peepal in Ahmedabad was cut down, Bharat Sisodia used a 50-tonne crane to lift and replant it nearly two kilometres away. It has since reportedly begun showing new growth, though no survival rate has been given.

sections.title: Not the first
paras: In Vasai, Sisodia's work linked to NHAI road construction helped relocate nearly 50 trees that faced removal. The Better India says costs were not disclosed.

stories.head: A Delhi fellowship pays rural performers a stipend to learn theatre
stories.dek: Bargad's six-month programme pays ₹10,000 a month, rising to ₹15,000 from January 2027, funded by individual donors.

sections.title: The fellowship
paras: Bargad runs a six-month theatre fellowship in Delhi, with classes from 4 pm to 8:30 pm six days a week and visiting faculty from Mumbai, Bengaluru and Chennai. The first cohort had 14 fellows, and the stipend was ₹10,000 a month for the first two cohorts and rises to ₹15,000 for the third, starting January 2027.

sections.title: Who pays
paras: About 20 to 25 individual donors have given between ₹5,000 and ₹5 lakh each over two years. The founders say they now want longer-term partners to keep it going. One participant said it was the first time he was paid to do theatre.

stories.head: After 28 years and 31,000 miles on foot, Karl Bushby is home in Hull
stories.dek: The former paratrooper reached home on 2 November and hugged his mother, Angela, at her gate.
stat: to walk around the world and back to Hull

sections.title: The walk
paras: Karl Bushby, 57, a former British paratrooper from Hull, set out in 1998 to walk around the world and return home entirely on foot. He arrived on 2 November 2026 after roughly 31,000 miles through 30 countries, and embraced his mother, Angela, saying '28 years! I could not have imagined this.'

sections.title: Along the way
paras: He crossed the Darien Gap, was arrested in Russia, swam more than 170 miles across the Caspian Sea to avoid Iran and Russia, and swam the English Channel after the Channel Tunnel operator refused to let him walk the service tunnel. In 2006 he and Dimitri Kieffer made the first recorded crossing of the frozen Bering Strait on foot.
